first: Ha, data cleaning will do that to you. Hope it went smoothly! Get some rest.

turns.user:
I'm good, let's keep going. Nice — I finished the helper columns. Next I want an Apps Script to speed two things:

1) Create a ParkMap sheet listing every distinct normalized park key (lowercase, non-letters removed) with a count of occurrences, so I can quickly fill the canonical name column.
2) After I fill canonical names in that ParkMap, run a script that writes the mapped canonical park back into the Clean!J column for all rows (and marks unmapped as "REVIEW").

Can you give that Apps Script (keep it minimal, ready to paste) plus a short note on where to run it and what permissions it needs?

Ran the script — works nicely. Two small tweaks please:

1) Change defaults to RAW_SHEET = "Clean" and keep CLEAN_COL = 10.
2) When building ParkMap, sort the keys by count descending (highest first).
3) Skip the final UI alert (or make it optional via a flag at top).

Can you paste the minimal updated script with those changes?

Nice — one more tweak: can you update the script so that after applyParkMap runs it also writes an "Unmapped" sheet listing every key that was mapped to "REVIEW" along with:
- the count of occurrences,
- up to 5 example row numbers (from Clean sheet) where that raw park value appears

That'll let me jump straight to problem values. Keep it minimal and ready to paste; same config constants at top (RAW_SHEET = "Clean", etc.). Also skip any UI alerts.

Nice — two small tweaks please:

1) In the Unmapped sheet, include up to 5 example raw park texts alongside the example row numbers (so columns: key, count, example_rows, example_texts).  
2) Remove the onOpen menu function (I run scripts from the editor).

Paste only the updated minimal script.

Nice — one more tweak: please treat empty/blank park entries as a tracked key (use key "<blank>") so they appear in Unmapped with count and example row numbers/texts. Keep everything else the same. Paste the updated minimal script ready to paste.

turns.text: Glad it all came together! You've got a solid cleaning pipeline now — normalized Yes/No, standardized phones and dates, deduplication flags, a formula-driven review column, and a fully scriptable park mapping workflow with unmapped tracking built in. Good luck with the rest of the volunteer data.
